facts.fact: The Swiss Re Foundation states that Guinea's rural Community Health Centers are often understaffed and rely on paper-based systems; it gives no date for this, so the page's published date is used.

Under the Clinic+O model, community health workers equipped with tablets and portable diagnostic devices capture patient information in an offline-first electronic medical record during screenings in communities and at Community Health Centers, with teleconsultation to remote physicians; the foundation gives no date, so the published date is used.
The Clinic+O electronic medical record is used in rural communities and at Community Health Centers, with no number of centres given; undated, so the published date is used.

The platform is run by Clinic+O, a non-profit founded in 2020, in collaboration with the Ministry of Health with a view to long-term integration into the public framework; undated, so the published date is used.
The Clinic+O project is funded by the Swiss Re Foundation as a 2026 Resilience Award project running November 2025 to December 2026; no domestic funding is mentioned.

A Swiss Re Foundation-funded Clinic+O project began in November 2025, to run to December 2026, extending the offline EMR and a dashboard of routine health-centre data for health workers and district supervisors.

systems.platform: offline-first electronic medical record on tablets, with dashboard and teleconsultation
systems.owner: Clinic+O (non-profit), in collaboration with the Ministry of Health; funded by Swiss Re Foundation
systems.tiers: rural communities (community health workers) and Community Health Centers; also supports the centres in digitising data collection and reporting into the national health information system
named only as the destination of community-level information

note: Classed emr because the document calls it an electronic medical record of patient information for general primary care; the operators are community health workers, so the parent may prefer class community.
